Is Oppenheimer Wrong to Give Up on Reddit? Wall Street Still Sees $150 ©Brett Jordan from Pexels via Canva and sasirin pamai's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Oppenheimer cut Reddit to Perform from Outperform on Oct. 30, removed its price target, and reissued the note on Nov. 13.

Reddit's third-quarter revenue rose 53%, but the company warned that daily users could fall this quarter as Alphabet's Google sends it less search traffic.

Wall Street's consensus target of $150 sits 51% above the price, and the stock trades at 12x forward earnings against a one-year average of 25x.

Oppenheimer's caution looks justified until 2027 earnings estimates stop falling and daily users find a floor.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) is 62% below its 52-week high, and Oppenheimer is in no hurry to buy the dip. The firm cut Reddit to Perform from Outperform on Oct. 30, the day after its third-quarter report, and removed its price target, citing uncertainty over Reddit's move to logged-in use and its Google relationship, according to TheFly. It reissued the note on Nov. 13.

Alphabet (GOOGL:NASDAQ) is a big part of the problem: its Google search is sending Reddit fewer visitors, and Reddit has warned that its daily users could shrink this quarter.

Search Traffic Is Falling Fast

Reddit's third-quarter revenue rose 53% to $895 million, and free cash flow nearly doubled to $363 million. But CEO Steve Huffman said on the Oct. 29 call that search referral traffic was "down meaningfully." In October, he added, "search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week."

If that keeps up, he said, "total DAUqs could fall in Q4 by a low double-digit percentage from our current base of 130 million DAUqs." And the fourth-quarter guide of $1 billion to $1.03 billion means revenue growth slows to about 40%.

Analysts Are Still Marking Reddit Down

Oppenheimer wasn't alone. KeyBanc and Citizens JMP downgraded Reddit the same day, Evercore ISI followed, and Loop Capital cut it to Hold with a $100 target on Nov. 2. Wall Street's average target came down with them:

RDDT Stock Mean Price Target: 1-Year (TIKR)

The consensus target is $150, down from $240 a year ago. Targets run from $100 to $272, and even the average sits 51% above the Nov. 12 close of $99.55.

Does $150 Add Up?

On estimates, Reddit still looks like a fast grower. Analysts expect normalized EPS of $7.72 this year and $9.29 in 2027, up from $4.54 in 2025:

RDDT Normalized EPS and Consensus Estimates: 2024-2028 (TIKR)

But the 2027 estimate was $9.68 in late October, before the report, and 2028's has dropped to $10.90 from $11.84. Investors are paying just 12x forward earnings, against a one-year average of 25x:

RDDT Stock NTM P/E: 1-Year (TIKR)

On 2028 estimates, $150 works out to about 14x, still well under that average. The multiple is this low because investors don't trust the estimates yet.

Should You Wait Before Buying Reddit Stock?

Reddit (RDDT) stock has lost 52.2% over the past twelve months, while the S&P 500 returned 12.2%. The shares now sit 61.6% below their January 2026 high, and on the October 29 call management warned that the number of people using Reddit each day could fall in the final quarter of 2026. Is $99.55 a low enough price to buy before Reddit shows whether it actually loses users?

Reddit Costs Less Than The S&P 500 On Earnings

Reddit trades at 19.3 times its earnings over the last twelve months, against 21.9 for the S&P 500. On sales the multiple has fallen sharply: buyers paid 22.7 times sales at the end of September 2025, and they pay 6.2 times today, still above the 3.2 for the S&P 500. That cheaper price comes with better margins, not worse ones. Reddit's operating margin over the twelve months to September 2026 was 29.4%, its highest at any of the 21 quarter ends since September 2021.

Profit is taxed lightly for now, with a tax rate of about 2% in the third quarter. That low rate lifts reported profit, so the earnings multiple would be higher at a normal tax rate. On cash, Reddit trades at 15.9 times operating cash flow, about level with 15.4 for the S&P 500, so on both measures Reddit is priced close to the market or below it.

The business kept growing, too: revenue rose 53% in the third quarter. Management's caution on the call was about users. Management said search referral traffic fell meaningfully in the quarter, with the decline speeding up late, and that Google is not sending people to Reddit the way it used to.

What Must Reddit Deliver In Its Fourth Quarter?

Reddit has guided fourth-quarter revenue of $1.0 billion to $1.03 billion, or 38% to 42% above a year earlier. The consensus for that quarter is $1.05 billion. With that figure sitting about $20 million above the top of the guide, the price appears to assume another beat. That sets a high bar for a company whose growth slowed in each quarter of 2026, dropping from 69.1% in the first to 53.0% in the third.

Management also warned about users. Search traffic dropped by more than 1 million referrals a week on average in October. If that pace continues, management said, daily users could fall in the fourth quarter by a low double-digit percentage from 130 million. Reddit will also begin testing a logged-in-only version in select markets outside the U.S. in the same quarter, which management said will likely trade reach for engagement.

Argus's $150 Target Says Reddit's Selloff Went Too Far ©@Brett Jordan from Pexels via Canva, @Karola G from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Argus cut its Reddit price target to $150 from $225 and kept its Buy rating, a target 49% above today's price.

Reddit's stock has sunk since its third-quarter report, when management warned that search traffic from Alphabet's Google is falling fast and daily users could drop.

At $150, Reddit would trade at about 18x forward earnings, well below its 25x average over the past year.

The selloff looks overdone, and Argus's target looks cautious, as long as 2027 earnings estimates stop sliding.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) stock has lost 59% since its January high, and on Nov. 12 Argus cut its price target to $150 from $225. It kept its Buy rating, and $150 is still 49% above today's price of $100.37.

The trouble is Alphabet (GOOGL:NASDAQ): Google is sending Reddit far fewer visitors as it answers more searches with AI.

Google's traffic is drying up

Reddit's third quarter, reported Oct. 29, looked great on paper, with revenue up 53% to $895 million. Then co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman told the call: "Our search referral traffic was down meaningfully in Q3, with the decline accelerating later in the quarter." He warned that daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter if the slide keeps up, and Reddit guided to fourth-quarter revenue growth of 38% to 42%.

Reddit also plans to go logged-in only, and Huffman admitted "we will likely be trading reach for engagement." Shares sank the next day.

Argus still likes the business

Argus analyst Joseph Bonner kept his Buy as he cut the target. His read is that the search-traffic warning overshadowed the quarter itself, and Argus raised its 2026 GAAP earnings estimate to $5.55 a share from $5.31, while holding 2027 at $6.54. Guggenheim made a similar call two days earlier, cutting to $140 and keeping its Buy.

Reddit is still generating plenty of cash. Free cash flow nearly doubled to $363 million in the third quarter, and Reddit bought back $100 million of its own stock at an average of $149.81 a share, almost exactly Argus's new target.

More on the Anthropic IPO: our Anthropic IPO storyline page collects our pieces on it.

The email arrives before your first coffee: "Indicate your interest in the Anthropic IPO." Your broker wants a share count by next week. You've used Claude at work for a year and you think it's the best AI there is. The form has one empty box, and it's asking how much.

Everyone knows the outline. Anthropic is expected to start trading on Nasdaq as ANT around November 19. On Tuesday it set a price range of $70 to $78 a share for 825 million shares: about $58 billion to $64 billion, at a value of $1.26 trillion to $1.41 trillion fully diluted.

Here's why the day matters less than the price. Most investors don't get shares at the offer price. They buy once trading opens, when the most excited buyers set it. SpaceX, the giant June listing, closed its first day 19% above its $135 offer. On Thursday it closed at $139.94.

That gap is the real decision. In the famous IPOs below, first-day buyers typically saw 25% drops within six months. In a portfolio of a few million dollars, is your entry plan ready? A Trefis partner firm can review it in a free 30-minute call.

title: Reddit Sinks 6% as Traffic Falls 13% on Google’s AI Overviews: “Not Traffic Drivers”

Reddit Sinks 6% as Traffic Falls 13% on Google’s AI Overviews: “Not Traffic Drivers”

Reddit Sinks 6% as Traffic Falls 13% on Google's AI Overviews: "Not Traffic Drivers" ©Brett Jordan from Pexels, Karola G from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Reddit shares fell 6% after Similarweb data showed a 13% drop in global visits, which Business Insider blamed on Google's AI Overviews.

Most of the lost visits were logged out, and the logged-in users behind over 80% of its monetization are still growing.

Pinterest's record user count and Meta's rising ad prices suggest advertisers keep paying for audiences that come back on their own.

Reddit's forward P/E is about half its one-year average, so the AI fear already looks priced in.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) is down 6% today after Business Insider reported that its global visits fell 13% from October 2025 to October 2026, according to Similarweb, and blamed Google's AI Overviews.

Two other ad platforms have a stake in this. Pinterest (PINS:NYSE) lists changes at search engines among its own risks. Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) sells ads to the kind of logged-in audience Reddit is now betting on.

The users who pay are still showing up

On Reddit's third-quarter call, CEO Steve Huffman said Google's AI Overviews "are not traffic drivers." U.S. daily active uniques fell to 50.7 million from 53.2 million in the second quarter. All of the drop came from logged-out users, and logged-in U.S. users rose 1% to 23.4 million.

COO Jen Wong said on the call that "over 80% of our monetization sits on the shoulders of logged-in in-app users." Third-quarter revenue rose 53% to $895 million. Analysts expect revenue to keep growing through 2028:

Reddit (RDDT): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

I don't think a count of mostly logged-out visits should make them cut those numbers.

Pinterest and Meta point the same way

Pinterest isn't showing the squeeze yet. Its monthly users hit a record 661 million in the third quarter, up 10%, and users in the U.S. and Canada rose 4% to 107 million. Monthly users aren't visits, though, so its report in early February will show whether Google is costing it traffic too.

Meta shows what logged-in users are worth. Its third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, and its price per ad rose 14%. That's the model Reddit is chasing as it pushes visitors to log in.

Reddit Inc. has seen its share price fall sharply this year, and the slide raises a straightforward question for investors who care about fundamentals. Is the current price tag on Reddit stock supported by what the business is earning today and what those earnings might reasonably deliver over time?

The share price is down 56.3% year to date, which puts the focus squarely on whether that reset lines up with the earnings power that Reddit is currently generating.

Management is pushing users toward a logged-in experience and new ad formats as search referral traffic falls, which can influence how quickly earnings grow and how predictable they become.

Your read on Reddit is one view; the desks covering it have another. See what analysts think Reddit's shares could be worth.

For investors, the debate is whether Reddit's latest share price reflects a fair multiple of its earnings given the user trends and monetization plan now in play.

If you are weighing Reddit's sharp year-to-date slide against its earnings story, it can help to compare that setup with other companies that screen as 32 high quality undervalued stocks.

Is Reddit Still Cheap on Earnings?

The P/E ratio fits Reddit because earnings are now positive and investors can at least anchor the share price to a real profit figure. Reddit trades at about 20.6x earnings, which is above the Interactive Media and Services sector average of roughly 9.0x but well below the peer group on about 37.8x.

The tailored fair multiple that blends Reddit's growth profile, margins, size and risks suggests a higher P/E than where the stock trades today, so the current 20.6x screens as undervalued on this framework. Because the sharp pullback followed concerns over slowing user growth and weaker guidance, the discount persists despite those risks already being front of mind for many investors.
